method: Each page rendered at 200 dpi with music_pages.py render, cropped to the recorded box (an exact crop and one with a 1% margin) and the box's text read against the recorded string, character for character. Apostrophes, the chord symbols and the superscripts were then checked in 300-600 dpi zooms. Line breaks, spacing and the "\n• " bullet were ignored, as instructed. Cross-check only, and the verdicts rest on the renders: the booklets' Calibri text is drawn by glyph id with no ToUnicode, so each box's glyphs were also decoded through a Calibri glyph-id-to-character map derived from sane ToUnicode sightings in 67 non-Music corpus PDFs, with the ligature ids taken from scripts/markbank/authoring/glyph_ids.json (302 = fi, 415 = ti, 859 = ’). Every decoded string matches the render, and every apostrophe in these boxes is glyph 859 (’), never 918 (the straight ').

entries.text: Excerpt 2, played three times. The opening lyrics are printed below. Line 1 Galileo, Galileo, Galileo, Galileo, Line 2 Galileo Figaro. Magnifico. Line 3 I’m just a poor boy, nobody loves me. Line 4 He’s just a poor boy from a poor family, Line 5 Spare him his life from this monstrosity.
entries.notes: Every word, comma and full stop matches, as do the labels Line 1 to Line 5 (Line 2 and Line 5 included) and the line order. "I’m" and "He’s" are printed with the curly ’ (600 dpi zoom; glyph id 859, the right single quotation mark, not 918, the straight quote). The box holds the heading and all five lines and nothing else.

entries.text: Excerpt 3, played three times. The lyrics are printed below. Line 1 Mama, just killed a man, Line 2 Put a gun against his head, pulled my trigger, now he’s dead. Line 3 Mama, life had just begun, Line 4 But now I’ve gone and thrown it all away.
differences: The page prints two boxed chord symbols above Line 1, inside the box, that the recorded text leaves out: "B♭" (a Calibri B with the flat drawn in the OpusTextStd music font) above "Mama," and "Gm" above "killed".
entries.notes: Apart from the chord symbols, everything matches: the heading, the labels Line 1 to Line 4, every word and punctuation mark, and the curly ’ in "he’s" and "I’ve" (glyph id 859). Typography only, not a character difference: "gun" in Line 2 is printed in bold (Calibri-Bold). The 2023 OL booklet prints the same four lines with no chord symbols and no bold.

Excerpt 2, played three times.
• The lyrics are printed below. Line 1 I never thought I’d miss you Line 2 Half as much as I do. Line 3 And I never thought I’d feel this way Line 4 The way I feel about you. Line 5 As soon as I wake up, every night every day. Line 6 I know that it’s you I need to take the blues away.
entries.notes: The heading, the bulleted "The lyrics are printed below.", the labels Line 1 to Line 6, every word and punctuation mark (including "every night every day." with no comma) and the curly ’ in "I’d" (twice) and "it’s" all match. Box only, not the text: the top edge (0.47) cuts through the heading "Excerpt 2, played three times.", which is printed at y 0.459-0.473, so the recorded text's first sentence sits almost wholly above the box. A top of about 0.45 would take it in.

entries.notes: The heading, the bulleted "The lyrics are printed below.", the labels Line 1 to Line 6, every word and punctuation mark, and the curly ’ in "I’d" (twice) and "it’s" all match. Box only, not the text: the recorded lines run from y 0.067 to 0.236, but the box (0.05-0.45) also takes in (c) "A feature of the vocal music heard in lines 1–4 is", its three options and the (d) stem.

Confirmed again: the second bullet reads "Use the form AA¹BB¹." with both 1s set superscript (6 pt glyphs on a raised baseline, zoomed at 600 dpi), and the full stop follows the second ¹. Spacing only, ignored as instructed: the page sets a 6 pt space glyph between "AA¹" and "BB¹", so it prints "AA¹ BB¹.". The box holds the lead-in and the first three bullets and cuts through the fourth. This agrees with the earlier confirmation in second-reader/2020-hl.json.
